cycleBasics.title: Cycle basics
cycleBasics.body: A cycle is counted from the first day of your period to the day before the next one. Lengths vary. Many people have cycles anywhere from about 21 to 40 days, and that range is wide.

questions.question: Which day counts as day 1 of a cycle?
options: The first day of your period
The day you first log a check-in
questions.explain: Day 1 is the first day of bleeding. Counting starts there and resets when the next period begins.

questions.question: What cycle length is common?
questions.explain: 28 days is a common average, not a rule. Lengths differ between people and from one cycle to the next.

questions.question: Why might keeping notes help?
options: It proves your cycle is perfect
It helps you notice your own patterns over time
It replaces talking to a clinician
questions.explain: Notes make patterns easier to see. Any worries are still worth raising with a clinician.

whatIsNormal.title: What is normal?
whatIsNormal.body: Normal varies a lot. Changes in flow, mood, or energy are common across a cycle. Changes that are new, persistent, or worrying are worth raising with a clinician, especially heavy bleeding, fever, or pain that stops you living your day.

questions.question: Is it normal for mood and energy to shift through the cycle?
options: No, they should be the same every day
questions.explain: Hormones shift across a cycle, so some change is common. What matters is whether it is new, persistent, or worrying.

questions.question: Which sign is a reason to see a clinician soon?
options: Soaking through protection every hour or two
questions.explain: Soaking through protection very often is a reason to get checked. One small change is usually fine to watch.

questions.question: What does a quiz score here mean?
options: Only how well you remember this lesson
questions.explain: Quizzes are for learning. They do not measure your health or your body.

talkingToClinician.title: Talking to a clinician
talkingToClinician.body: Bring clear notes: when things started, how often they happen, and what helps. You can ask for more time, ask for a second opinion, and ask questions at any pace.

questions.question: What is useful to bring to an appointment?
options: Notes on timing, flow, and symptoms
Only a guess at your age
questions.explain: Clear dates and details help your clinician understand what is happening.

questions.question: You feel rushed in an appointment. What can you do?
options: Ask for more time or write your questions down
questions.explain: You are allowed to ask for time and to say what you need in order to understand.

questions.question: Does this app replace medical advice?
options: No, it supports you alongside a clinician
questions.explain: HerCycle is a companion for learning and notes. It is not a diagnosis, and it never replaces a clinician.
